reason: E1 directly supports the first three premises by showing deformation-induced segregation in MoNbTaTiV that appears at low temperature/high strain rate and disappears at high temperature/low strain rate, attributed to dislocation movement. However, the cited evidence does not address the link between segregation and fracture mode (premises 4 and 5); E2 discusses grain boundary serration and ductility in a different alloy system without measuring segregation, so it does not support the proposed mechanism of segregation-induced brittle failure.
premises: Deformation-induced elemental segregation occurs at grain boundaries in single-phase HEAs
Segregation is promoted by low temperature and high strain rate
Segregation is mitigated by high temperature and low strain rate due to dislocation movement
Grain boundary segregation reduces local cohesive strength and promotes brittle intergranular fracture
Homogeneous grain boundary composition correlates with ductile transgranular fracture
